name: prism-vault-restore
title: Prism Vault Restore
purpose: Decides whether bytes read back from the browser vault may be handed out, so that tampered, swapped or unreadable objects are refused and hash-only records never come back as values.

fields.name: key
fields.means: whether the browser still holds the vault's own non-extractable key

fields.name: format
fields.means: whether the stored envelope has a version this vault reads

fields.name: seal
fields.means: whether the AES-GCM seal, bound to the object's address, opened

fields.name: address
fields.means: whether the opened bytes re-derive to the address they were read from

fields.name: kind
fields.means: whether the record holds a value or only a hash and pointer

rules.says: when key is missing then refuse
when format is unknown then refuse
when seal is broken then refuse
when address is mismatch then refuse
when kind is hash then hashonly
when kind is value then restore

properties.says: always when address is mismatch then refuse
properties.why: stored bytes must re-derive to their address, or they could stand in for another object

properties.says: always when seal is broken then refuse
always when key is missing then refuse
properties.why: nothing is readable without the key

properties.says: never when format is unknown then restore
properties.why: an envelope the vault cannot read is never guessed at

properties.says: never when kind is hash then restore
properties.why: a hash-only record never turns back into a value

meanings.hashonly: hand out only the hash and pointer
meanings.refuse: hand out nothing and report the object as damaged

limits: It does not open the seal or hash the bytes; the adapter does that with WebCrypto and reports the result.
A refused object stays on disk for the owner to inspect; the adapter never deletes it on its own.
